_note: Since you cannot run a real browser, use code analysis to detect common layout issues.

check_1_unwrapped_visuals.pattern: Visual elements (,

check_2_missing_spacing: Images/videos should have margin: 2rem 0 or be wrapped in a container with that margin.
Chart containers should have vertical spacing.
Stat callouts should have spacing above and below.
check_3_centering: Images should have display: block; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto or be in a centered container.
Charts should be centered within their max-width constraint.

Chart RENDER OUTPUT must be centered, not just the container: center the rendered SVG with `.vega-embed svg{display:block;margin:0 auto}` on each vegaEmbed mount's shared chart class, because faceted/concat/step charts ignore width:container, render narrower than the mount, and otherwise left-align. NEVER set `.vega-embed{display:inline-block}` to center — an inline-block wrapper is shrink-to-fit, so Vega measures the container width as 0 and the chart renders at 0×H (invisible). Find mounts with grep -n 'vegaEmbed' index.html and check each.

No chart renders at 0 width: if a vegaEmbed mount produces an <svg> with width 0 (or stays visually blank with reserved height), its mount or .vega-embed is shrink-to-fit (display:inline-block / float / inline) and has collapsed width:"container" to 0 — force the mount and .vega-embed to display:block; width:100%.
Full-bleed / breakout visuals should use viewport-based centering and must clear inherited max-width from wrappers like figure.visual-container.
check_4_responsive: Images should have max-width: 100%; height: auto.
No fixed widths that exceed 720px (except full-width teasers).
Charts should use "width": "container" in Vega specs.
Timelines or step sequences should not rely on 1000px+ fixed-width absolute layouts inside the story column.

check_5_inline_provenance_island_byte_id.pattern: The page reads the INLINE <script type="application/json"> provenance islands (verifyMap / runCells), not the on-disk verify/*.json. Extract each inline island's text and byte-compare it to verify/verify_map.json and verify/run_cells.json — they MUST be byte-identical. Any mismatch = stale provenance in the drawer (re-inline from the verify/*.json source; never hand-edit the island).

check_6_multi_asset_gallery_not_firsturl.pattern: An entry whose media is an array (flags / assets / photos / multi-value source_url) must render a GALLERY — every asset gets its own thumbnail + label + source link + license. Flag any renderer that reduces a multi-asset array to its first element via firstUrl(...) or [0]; multi-asset entries must map over the whole array, not just index 0.

check_7_runcells_pyodide_safe_imports.pattern: Every runnable (Pyodide) snippet in run_cells.json must import ONLY numpy / pandas / stdlib, be self-contained (no file or network reads), and reduced-N. Flag any runnable snippet importing a package outside {numpy, pandas, stdlib}, any file/network read, and any cell with needs_network:true while runnable:true (that combo must be runnable:false). Reduced-N cells must be graded '≈ within noise', never a hard PASS. DTYPE SAFETY (PIT-63): Pyodide's numpy is a 32-bit wasm build (np.intp=int32), so np.bincount( (and other platform-intp index sinks) THROW casting int64->int32 on an int64 array — though the identical cell passes in local 64-bit Python. Flag a runnable cell calling np.bincount( on an arg not wrapped in np.intp (np.asarray(x,dtype=np.intp)); validate.py Section 18 raises pyodide_int64_dtype_trap deterministically and this is the Auditor's grep mirror. And require runnable cells be smoke-tested in REAL Pyodide (the in-page 'Run' button), not just local Python — local success does not prove in-browser success.

check_8_notebook_local_reproducible.pattern: The reproducible notebook must run by DOWNLOAD-AND-RUN-LOCALLY (there is NO Colab branch — do not require or expect IN_COLAB / REPO_RAW_BASE). It must (a) carry NO hardcoded absolute path (no drive-letter path like D:\..., no leading /home/ or /Users/) and (b) resolve its inputs through a DATA_DIR resolver (env-var override -> repo-relative -> absolute, FIRST that resolves) so a reader who downloads the notebook + the bundled verify/data/ inputs can run it as-is. Flag a hardcoded absolute path, or a missing DATA_DIR resolver. Do NOT flag the absence of a Colab/IN_COLAB/REPO_RAW_BASE fetch branch — that branch has been removed by design.

check_9_hero_ai_video_web_weight.pattern: The referenced hero / AI-generated video must be web-weight: each referenced .mp4 <= 3 MB (H.264) with a .webm twin. Stat every video file referenced from index.html and flag any > 3 MB (raw generator output is typically 20-30 MB and must be transcoded via ffmpeg / static-ffmpeg before shipping); confirm the page points at the transcoded web copy, not the raw original.

check_10_video_model_misuse._ref: flagship_contract.json hero_video_continuous_backdrop (E5); designer media_presentation.json; report_types.json hero_video_hard_cut
check_10_video_model_misuse.pattern: Video-generation model misuse. (a) An image2video / i2v clip MUST request a model-SUPPORTED duration (the generators expose ONLY 4 / 6 / 8 s — any other `duration` is silently clamped or rejected, shipping a wrong-length or missing clip): flag any designer video `duration` not in {4,6,8}. (b) An AI video MUST NOT pose as a specific real object/place/person (a faked trophy/stadium/anthem) — that is the image-viewing test in Step 1b, not a grep. (c) When the hero is a VIDEO and the page is cinematic, the video must hand off to a CONTINUOUS backdrop (the next scene's first frame / a held last-frame still / a crossfade), NOT a hard fade-to-black cut that strands the reader on an empty frame — flag a hero <video> followed immediately by a blank/hard-cut section with no continuous-backdrop bridge. Send the duration/handoff defects to the Designer (regenerate at a supported duration / author the backdrop handoff).

check_11_decorative_data_provenance._ref: validate.py Section 9 (decorative_carries_data_id); inspector inspector_panel_internals.json decorative_skip; report_types.json decorative_carries_provenance
check_11_decorative_data_provenance.pattern: A DECORATIVE overlay — an element whose OWN inline style sets `pointer-events:none` (a non-interactive chip / floating canvas / scrim) — must NOT carry a provenance `data-{ana,det,des,sct,cin,int}` token. A decorative node with a data-* id pollutes the provenance graph: the Inspector opens a drawer for a thing that is not a claim, and validate.py demands a verify_map entry for it. NOTE the legitimate pattern is NOT a violation: `data-cin`/`data-sct` belongs on the VISIBLE <section>/beat whose CHILD scrim/img is the pointer-events:none layer — token and pointer-events:none live on DIFFERENT elements. Flag only a SINGLE element that carries BOTH on itself. validate.py Section 9 enforces this deterministically; this is the Auditor's grep mirror. Send back to the Programmer (move the data-* to the real visible element it describes).

(a) WIDTH CAP (unchanged): for each block, confirm the (or its figure) carries a `max-width` (e.g. `max-width:100%;height:auto`) or an explicit `width`, OR is covered by a global `img{max-width:100%}` in the page

check_13_photographic_gradient_rest_blac._ref: validate.py Section 6c (cin_photographic_gradient_rest / cin_consecutive_gradient_rests); cinematographer cinematic_recipes.json pinned_crossfade.continuous_photo_no_black_gap_CRITICAL; component_implementations.json cinematic_background (photographic rest = dimmed real photo)
check_13_photographic_gradient_rest_blac.pattern: Near-black gradient REST creates a black scroll gap in PHOTOGRAPHIC cinematic mode (a photo ends -> near-black gradient section -> long scroll -> next photo). When cinematographer.json meta.mode is `photographic` (or the legacy alias `cinematic`), NO cin scene may be a `kind:gradient`/`kind:color` rest, and no two consecutive scenes may both be gradient rests — a photographic rest must HOLD a dimmed/framed REAL sct_/des_ photo (reuse the `framed` blurred-fill), so a real image is always on screen, crossfading into the next. Flag (a) any cin scene with background.kind gradient|color while meta.mode is photographic/cinematic, and (b) two adjacent `.cin-bg` background layers in index.html that paint a CSS `linear-gradient`/`radial-gradient` and carry NO data-sct/data-des (gradient layers carry data-cin only) — that pair is the back-to-back black-gap. validate.py Section 6c ERRORs on this deterministically (photographic mode only — generative/data_driven legitimately use gradient/atmosphere rests); this is the Auditor's grep mirror. Send back to the Cinematographer (redefine the rest as a dimmed real photo) / Programmer (render the dimmed real-photo layer, not a bare gradient).

check_14_chart_interaction_robustness_fl._ref: validate.py Section 14 (chart_no_fault_isolation / chart_no_cdn_fallback); render_capture.js findings.cascadeScriptAbort / findings.brokenMaps / findings.zeroWidthBars; component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite.{fault_isolation_RULE,no_sentinel_baseline_RULE,responsive_embed} + maps_leaflet FM4 + interactive_elements FM1/FM2/FM5; report_types.json chart_cascade_script_abort / chart_no_fault_isolation / chart_sentinel_deref / chart_no_cdn_fallback / map_sizing_invalidate
check_14_chart_interaction_robustness_fl.pattern: The deterministic chart/interaction-robustness floor for a browserless box (the real-browser audits skip to UNVERIFIED when no Chrome is present, so these greps are the no-render fallback). Five failure modes: (FM1 fault isolation) all charts/interactions are emitted into ONE shared inline <script> run sequentially — the FIRST synchronous uncaught throw aborts the whole block, blanking every later chart AND the hero; confirm each chart/playground setup is its OWN `(function(){ try{…}catch(e){console.error(...)} })()` IIFE (a single <script> with >=2 `vegaEmbed(`/setup mounts but <1 `try` is the smell). render_capture.js findings.cascadeScriptAbort (console error + >=2 blanked charts) is ground truth. (FM2 sentinel/null deref) flag a baseline render called with a sentinel a callee derefs — `draw(null,…)`/`render(null)`/`update(undefined)` — and any `Number(`/`parseFloat(` applied to an attribute that can be a `{value,flag}` object (→ NaN → width:NaN% paints nothing, PIT-05); render_capture findings.zeroWidthBars is ground truth. (FM3 re-render gap) a width:container chart must go through the `embedChart` helper that re-paints on first-visible (IntersectionObserver/ResizeObserver), not just resize — a chart starting in a display:none/0-box tab/accordion/cinematic-revealed beat stays blank otherwise. (FM4 Leaflet sizing) a Leaflet map needs a fixed container height before init + `map.invalidateSize()` on first-visible + debounced resize, else it renders grey/0-tile; render_capture findings.brokenMaps (>0 mount, 0 tiles, or 0-height .leaflet-container) is ground truth — confirm an `invalidateSize` call exists when `L.map(` is used. (FM5 CDN-load + handler guards) a chart/map page using the Vega/Leaflet CDN must guard `typeof vegaEmbed!=='function'` / `typeof L==='undefined'` and fall back to a static inlined-data <table>, and wrap every feature-side interaction handler body in try/catch (edge-value-safe). validate.py Section 14 WARNs `chart_no_fault_isolation` + `chart_no_cdn_fallback` deterministically (ERROR on a computational/rich topic); this is the Auditor's grep mirror. Route correctness defects to the Programmer (wrap each setup in a try/catch IIFE, guard nulls/edge values, add the invalidateSize + CDN fallback).

check_15_titling_caption_quality._ref: data2story/copywriter/SKILL.md (AT1-AT9 kill-list + D1-D16 devices + caption takeaway-rule); critic rubric.json narrative_pacing.titling_caption_cap; report_types.json titling_generic_headline / caption_states_no_finding; frontend-design/references/exemplars/titling_captioning.md
check_15_titling_caption_quality.pattern: ADVISORY titling/captioning-quality grep (the Copywriter's gate; soft — it never hard-blocks the build and is intentionally NOT a validate.py kind yet, so the deterministic contract gate stays clean until the rule is proven two-sided). Three checks, each routed to the **copywriter**. (a) TEMPLATED / AI-TELL HEADLINE (PIT-56): grep the <h1> (and section <h2>) for the AT1 two-beat — a flat declarative sentence immediately followed by a short contradicting one ('Argentina is the favourite. No bookmaker agrees.' / a 'X. Not Y.' / 'not X, it's Y' shape: a `. ` mid-heading then a <=5-word counter-clause) — and for the templated roots 'An Analysis of', 'A Look at', 'Exploring ', 'Understanding ', a reflexive colon subtitle ('Word: A … of …'), and an empty superlative ('the most '/'-est') with no backing number; flag a hit → report_types titling_generic_headline. (b) STANDFIRST PRE-SPOIL (PIT-57): if interaction.json declares a centerpiece (hero) whose reveal number is a distinctive figure (>=3 digits, from analyst.json/interaction.json), grep the masthead standfirst/dek for that exact number appearing verbatim — a dek stating the number the hero exists to make the reader PRODUCE is the spoiler (dedup with the Editor's standfirst check; route once to copywriter). (c) CAPTION LABELS-AN-AXIS (PIT-58): grep every <figcaption> for the forbidden openers — 'Figure \d', 'This (chart|figure) shows', 'the x-axis', 'the y-axis', 'is pictured', 'poses', 'looks on', 'may suggest a possible' — and for a caption that is only an axis/type label rather than a stated finding; flag a hit → report_types caption_states_no_finding. (d) MARKETING WORD in any h1/h2/figcaption: grep for novel / state-of-the-art / unprecedented / groundbreaking / revolutionary / first-to. The Critic corroborates all four via rubric.json narrative_pacing.titling_caption_cap (cap narrative_pacing at 3). Send every hit back to the **copywriter** (re-title the masthead / section / caption in copywriter.json — naming, not editing; no finding/number/id changes). The greps must be CLEAN on a Copywriter-titled flagship build and HIT on a crafted templated title — a grep clean-but-unable-to-hit is a dead detect.
